title.narrative: Emergency Food Aid in Northern West Bank Area

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to address urgent food needs of vulnerable IDPs affected by military operations in Jenin and Tulkarm. It supports the 2025 Humanitarian Flash Appeal and FSS objectives by improving food security through timely and adequate food assistance, particularlyltbgt via a mixed-modality approach of e-vouchers and in-kind fresh foodlt/bgt, ensuring access to essential nutrition for displaced families in the northern West Bank. ltbrgtltbgtThe project will also ensure including fresh vegetables and fruits that will be sourced from small-scale farmers who are vulnerable, struggling to sell, and farming in marginalized areas in coordination with local stakeholders such as CBOs and cooperatives which will be selected accordingly to ensure direct support to these farmers. This setup will help inject value into local production chains. lt/bgtThe project is coordinated with a holistic approach to cover food urgent and basic needs in a complementary way with all relevant stakeholders, including OCHA, UNRWA, local stakeholders (emergency committees), and MoSD. ACF will target the most urgent food needs of the most vulnerable IDPs in affected areas based on specified and agreed selection criteria among stakeholders. The project is coordinated with PARC, the second implementer within this allocation, where ACF and PARC will cover both governorates based on the final list and the IDPs’ locations. ltbgtThe project contributes to food security among the most affected IDPs by providing basic food items. It also supports vulnerable small-scale farmers by sourcing fresh vegetables and fruits directly from them for in-kind distribution to the same households receiving e-vouchers, thereby supporting dual objectives of food security and economic resilience. lt/bgtThe project has ltbgt4 main activitieslt/bgt 1) coordination and finalizing the targeted list, ltbgt2) identifying and selecting ways to source items from small scale farmers/food producers,lt/bgt 3) ltbgtDisbursement of assistance through ILS 280 e-vouchers for food items and in-kind distribution of fresh food valued at ILS 70,lt/bgt 4) Monitoring and evaluation, including post-distribution monitoringltbgt (PDM) after each roundlt/bgt. lt/pgtltpgtThe prime activity will be the distribution of ltbgtILS 280 e-voucherslt/bgt ltbgtper HH per month for three monthslt/bgt. ltbgtIn parallel, HHs will receive fresh vegetables and fruits via in-kind distributionlt/bgt, ltbgtsourcedlt/bgt from affected ltbgtsmall-scale farmers, cooperatives, or CBOslt/bgt depending on ltbgtlocation and market accesslt/bgt. ACF will select the ltbgtmost appropriate modality for fresh food delivery, in-kind, vouchers, or coupons, based on access constraints, security conditions, and beneficiary preferences.ltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtThe project prioritizes IDPs with no access to food inside camps, returnees, and those in shelters lacking cooking facilities or clean water. It targets households not covered by MPCA, those impacted by military operations, and families facing income loss or market access constraints. Special attention is given to female-headed households, large families, and individuals with disabilities, children, or elderly dependentslt/bgt. The project will complement other interventions and avoid duplication of assistance and ensure that food needs of most affected are met within the suggested timeframe. lt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will target ltbgt1429lt/bgt HHs in both governorates (ltbgt715 lt/bgtHHs in Jenin and ltbgt714lt/bgt HHs in Tulkarm) ltbgtwith a monthly food support valued at ILS 350 for 3 rounds, split into ILS 280 for restricted e-vouchers and ILS 70 for fresh food. lt/bgtltbrgtACF will coordinate with UNRWA and stakeholders to verify and finalize beneficiary lists, ensuring flexibility in food assistance modalities based on access constraints. The project integrates protection principles and accountability to promote safety, dignity, and participation. Continuous monitoring and PDM will guide implementation and adjustments, improving food security and reducing vulnerabilities among IDPs.ltbrgtlt/pgt
